final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mostly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is directionally more accurate because it concedes that monitoring, rollback, and limited rollout do not cure the exposed weak segment. But that narrower position still does not satisfy the governing policy. The admissible evidence shows the affected insurance claims triage use case remains exposed in launch, and there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. The policy text states that rollout controls and post-launch monitoring can mitigate a material weakness only if they exclude the affected use case or include reviewed risk acceptance; a rollback switch, dashboard, or small initial percentage does not remove disclosure duties when the segment remains exposed. This is not a case for compliant_with_caveats, because the missing exclusion-or-approved-risk-acceptance condition is itself the unresolved compliance predicate, not a minor caveat around an otherwise satisfied requirement.
remaining_concerns: The insurance claims triage segment remains below target on catastrophe claim evidence triage and is still included in the initial rollout cohort.

The policy allows rollout controls and monitoring to mitigate a material weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable; neither is in evidence.
The available risk-acceptance document is only a draft, has no approver, and does not mention the exposed insurance claims triage segment.
Rollback capability, 9% initial rollout, and monitoring are relevant operational controls but do not satisfy the specific policy predicate while the affected segment remains exposed.
Generic public guidance on model cards and AI risk management does not override the stricter internal release-policy requirement.
